 Zach LaVine 
 SAC 
 Guard 
 #8 
 Personalize your Rotoworld feed by favoriting players 
 Zach LaVine recorded 15 points (6-of-10 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, two assists and one three-pointer in Sunday’s loss to the Heat. 
 LaVine shot the ball well on Sunday, but the playing time was an eye-opener. He played 25 minutes against the Heat and did not return after being subbed out with 4:03 remaining in the third quarter. The Kings made no injury announcement, and LaVine was called for one foul, so foul trouble couldn’t have been the reason. Kings head coach Doug Christie played Darius Acuff Jr. and Malik Monk (9/2/3/1) in the backcourt for the entire fourth quarter, which left no room for LaVine. That’s something for fantasy managers to watch moving forward. 
 Dylan Cardwell 
 SAC 
 Center 
 #32 
 Darius Acuff Jr., Zach LaVine, De’Andre Hunter, Precious Achiuwa and Dylan Cardwell will start Sunday’s game against the Heat. 
 The Kings are without Domantas Sabonis (knee) for Sunday’s game, opening up a spot in the starting lineup. Cardwell will replace him, and the Kings will need his rebounding and defense. Also, Hunter reclaims his place in the lineup with Leaky Black heading to the bench. And Achiuwa remains in the starting lineup despite Keegan Murray returning from an ankle injury. 
 De'Andre Hunter 
 SAC 
 Forward-Guard 
 #15 
 De’Andre Hunter (illness) is not on the injury report for Sunday’s game against the Heat. 
 Hunter did not play in Friday’s loss to the Spurs, with Leaky Black replacing him in the starting lineup. Black has played significant minutes recently due to his defensive ability, and that should remain the case on Sunday. 
 Leaky Black 
 SAC 
 Forward 
 #19 
 Leaky Black put up 12 points (4-of-7 FGs), three rebounds, five assists, two steals and four three-pointers in a loss to the Spurs on Friday. 
 Leaky Black led the team in minutes in this game which goes to show how much Christie likes him. The Kings don’t have many wing defenders at the moment, and the wings they have that have size are currently injured. Black had moments with the Hornets and Wizards prior to this season with the Kings. If you’re in a deep dynasty league and he’s available, I’d take a look because he’s playing minutes right now, and what he provides does have some value. 
 Darius Acuff 
 SAC 
 Guard 
 #5 
 The Sacramento Kings will start Darius Acuff, Zach LaVine, Leaky Black, Precious Achiuwa, and Domantas Sabonis on Friday. 
 DeAndre Hunter (illness) will not play against the Spurs on Friday, so Leaky Black will get the start. Leaky has been an energy guy who has gained some favor in the eyes of Doug Christie. If you’re in a deeper league, Leaky Black could be worth a stream, but the ball won’t be in his hands with this current iteration of the Kings. 
 De'Andre Hunter 
 SAC 
 Forward-Guard 
 #15 
 De’Andre Hunter (illness) is questionable for Friday’s matchup with the Spurs. 
 With Keegan Murray (ankle) still on the shelf, Sacramento’s rotation is already thin. If Hunter is forced to sit out against San Antonio, Emanuel Sharp and Malik Monk could handle additional minutes. 
 Malik Monk 
 SAC 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Malik Monk had 13 points (5-of-16 FGs), two rebounds, three assists, and three 3-pointers in loss to Lakers. 
 Malik Monk is currently shooting 35.1% from the field on the season which is currently a career low, including his rookie season. He has really struggled to get into a rhythm and the Kings are not as interested in playing and utilizing his skillset. He should start hitting more shots, but the disinterest in the organization to play him isn’t a great sign for his long term future in the league. 
 Dylan Cardwell 
 SAC 
 Center 
 #32 
 Dylan Cardwell (calf) is not on the injury report for Wednesday’s game against the Lakers. 
 Cardwell will be available to make his season debut on Wednesday after missing time with a calf strain. His return may mean less playing time for Leaky Black, who logged 25 minutes in Monday’s win over the Mavericks. 
 Malik Monk 
 SAC 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Malik Monk amassed 24 points (9-of-14 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), one rebound, seven assists, one block and five three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Mavericks. 
 After totaling 19 points in his first five appearances of the season, Monk snapped out of that funk in a major way on Monday. The Kings’ bench sparkplug scored 11 points in the first half and 13 in the second, and no one will turn down Monk’s seven assists, either. Also, he played a season-high 30 minutes on Monday. If Monk continues to play mid-to-high 20s minutes, his chances of providing reliable deep-league fantasy value increase. 
 Zach LaVine 
 SAC 
 Guard 
 #8 
 Zach LaVine (elbow) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Mavericks. 
 LaVine is dealing with right elbow inflammation. He hasn’t missed a game this season, but if that changes, Malik Monk could take on a bigger role, whether he starts or comes off the bench.

 Cade Cunningham led the Pistons with 52 points (16-of-25 FGs, 17-of-18 FTs), five rebounds, 11 assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in a 144-140 double overtime win over the Wizards on Thursday.
 Cunningham set a new career high for scoring in this game, with 30 of those 52 coming in the fourth quarter and overtime. However, the most impressive part of his performance was that he didn’t turn the ball over once, which led to him becoming the first player with at least 50 points and 10 assists in a game without turning it over. This was one of the best games anyone has had this season, and it came after he scored a total of 31 points over Detroit’s last two games. It was good to see him not only get back on track, but to truly dominate. He’ll look to carry some of this production with him to Miami on Saturday to wrap up the week.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Daniss Jenkins lit up the Wizards with 21 points (6-of-11 FGs), six rebounds, two steals and three three-pointers on Thursday.
 Jenkins has been on fire as of late, which continued in this game. This was the third straight game that he scored at least 20 points, with the last two coming as a starter. He didn’t have any assists in this game, but he has been productive as a playmaker this year and had a season high eight dimes in their last game on Monday. Jenkins has played well enough that he may remain a starter when Jalen Duren is healthy.

 Edgecombe did a little bit of everything for Philadelphia in this game. He set a new season high for assists while stuffing the stat sheet in the win. Edgecombe’s production has dropped off from his rookie season, which was expected. However, he is still able to produce well-rounded value, and when other starters miss time, his usage leaps up, which allows him to provide numbers like he did in this game.

 Joel Embiid lit up the Raptors on Thursday with 20 points (7-of-17 FGs), four rebounds, three assists, one steal and two blocks.
 Embiid banged knees with Ja’Kobe Walter in the first quarter, which forced him to exit the game briefly. Thankfully, he wasn’t gone long and was able to finish out the game. This was his fifth 20-point game of the season, though he did finish with a season-low four rebounds.  Tyrese Maxey led the 76ers with 27 points (8-of-13 FGs, 10-of-12 FTs), two rebounds, eight assists, two steals, one block and one three-pointer in a 123-112 win over the Raptors on Thursday.
 Maxey started this game off hot, scoring 10 points in the first quarter alone, which propelled his team-high scoring outing. Maxey is now averaging 26 points while shooting 61 percent from the floor over the last three games, which is a strong stretch after two rough performances where he shot below 35 percent from the floor prior to this. Maxey will look to keep it going against the Pacers on Sunday to wrap up the week.

 RJ Barrett led the Raptors with 31 points (13-of-20 FGs), 14 rebounds, five assists and four three-pointers in a 123-112 loss to the 76ers on Thursday.
 After a couple rough shooting nights, Barrett was able to get back on track in this game. He has scored at least 20 points in nine of his 12 games this season, though he had failed to reach that mark in his two previous games. He ended up setting a new season high for scoring in this one, and he fell one rebound shy of matching his career high. It was a spectacular night for Barrett as he tried to keep the shorthanded Raptors in the game.

 Collin Murray-Boyles finished with 14 points (5-of-9 FGs), four assists, one steal, five blocks and one three-pointer against the 76ers on Thursday.
 Murray-Boyles is starting to pick up the production after a rough start to the season. He set a new season high for blocks in this game and has at least one swat in three straight games. CMB hasn’t popped like many managers were hoping for, but he is beginning to produce high-level value in multiple categories. Entering the starting unit has helped, which will hopefully allow him to keep it going as the season continues, even if he eventually moves back to the bench.

 Immanuel Quickley lit up the 76ers on Thursday with 26 points (8-of-16 FGs, 7-of-8 FTs), four rebounds, six assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers.
 After being held to a season-low 11 points on Wednesday, Quickley got back on track in this one. He fell one point shy of matching his season high for scoring, which was the only other game he has shot at least 50 percent from the floor this season. It has been a solid season so far for Quickley despite his field goal percentage being rough to this point. He’ll look to build off this one with the Knicks coming to Toronto on Sunday.
